subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.

spec.name: Convoy Hauler Aegis-7
spec.description: A low-poly cyberpunk six-wheeled armoured hauler with a bristling cab and a neon-lit sealed cargo pod strapped to its flatbed.
spec.layout: Long heavy truck facing +Z. Front: sloped armoured cab nose with a wedge bull-bar, a cyan visor strip, twin amber headlights and a grille (z 3.0 to 4.2). Cab body sits above the front axle (z 1.4 to 3.0, y 0.9 to 2.3) with a roof turret ring at the top. Behind the cab a long flatbed chassis (z -4.2 to 1.2, deck top y 1.2) rests on a rear tandem of wheels and carries the big rounded-box cargo pod (z -3.9 to 0.9, y 1.3 to 2.9), strapped down with hazard-yellow bands and glowing magenta seal lines. Wheels: 2 at the front axle, 4 at the rear tandem, chunky, with hub glow rings. Faceted hulls in dark gunmetal with yellow hazard trim, cyan and magenta neon edges, panelled paints with rivets and grime near the wheels. Everything is blocky and angular, with textures for hazard stripes, decals, screens and glyphs.

parts.builds: Ladder frame and flatbed deck: two long side rails, cross-members, deck plate with hazard-stripe edge texture and panelled paint, side fuel tanks and tool lockers with rivets, underbody drive shaft and axle housings (hubs excluded), fenders over every wheel, mud flaps, rear bumper with warnRed tail lights and a magenta under-glow strip, side skirts with neon cyan edge lines.
parts.attaches: Deck top at deckTop carries the pod; cab body starts at cabRear; axle lines at rearAxle1/2 and frontAxle receive wheels.

parts.builds: Front axle pair and the middle left and right wheels: chunky faceted tyres with tread blocks, steel rims with bolt rings, glowing cyan hub caps (glow), brake discs and suspension arms. Mud-stained paint near the ground. Each wheel on its own wheel joint.
parts.attaches: Wheels sit on mounts frontAxle and rearAxle1 and ride joints wheelFL, wheelFR, wheelML, wheelMR.

parts.builds: Rear axle pair wheels plus the tandem walking beam suspension: tyres, tread, rims, bolt rings, magenta glowing hub caps, leaf spring packs and shock absorbers linking to the chassis, rear mud guards. Tyres grimy with paint.
parts.attaches: Sits on mount rearAxle2, rides wheelBL and wheelBR, springs reach up to the chassis at deckTop minus the rail.

parts.builds: The armoured cab body: angular faceted box with sloped roof and armour plates, panelled paint with rivets and hazard-stripe trim, side doors with handles, side windows (glass colour with a cyan reflection texture), roof rails with antennas, spotlight bar, exhaust stacks behind the cab, a rear cab wall with a glowing screen. Interior seats and dashboard visible through glass with a small glowing display texture.
parts.attaches: Rests on chassis at cabRear and front face meets noseFace; roof at cabRoof holds the turret ring.

parts.builds: The nose of the hauler: sloped armoured hood wedge, big grille with horizontal slats and a neon cyan frame, two amber glowing headlights with bracket housings, magenta fog light strips, a cyan visor windscreen with an SVG HUD-style texture, a heavy angular bull-bar bumper with yellow-black hazard paint and a tow hook, a faction emblem decal on the hood, front mud guards and side mirrors.
parts.attaches: Back face meets cabShell at noseFace z 3.0 and chassis front frame.

parts.builds: Roof-mounted remote weapon station: a ring base, rotating faceted armoured housing with a glowing cyan sensor eye and camera lens decal, twin barrels with muzzle brakes and heat-vent sleeves, ammo box with a belt feed, shield plates with hazard trim, small antenna and warning light. Housing rides turretYaw; barrels and sensor ride gunPitch.
parts.attaches: Base ring sits on cabRoof at turretRing.

parts.builds: The sealed cargo pod: a big rounded-faceted capsule container in podShell with dark podDark end caps, panelled paint with grime, glowing magenta seal-line seams and a glowing lock plate, hazard-yellow tie-down straps with ratchets and chains to the deck, a hatch (on podHatch) on top with a warning-red beacon, SVG decals of biohazard-style glyphs, serial numbers and corp logo, a small status display texture, side handles and corner brackets, and roof cable conduits.
parts.attaches: Rests on chassis deck at deckTop / podFloor; front stops short of cabRear at z 1.0.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning a single function to build the nose, keeping it concise while being careful about the Ctx type and its expected shape so I don't accidentally redeclare something the module already provides.

Now I'm sketching the geometry: a hood wedge extruded along the x-axis from a sloped side profile, plus a tilted windscreen plate positioned at the cab's front, working out the exact coordinates for where the hood dips down and the glass angles upward.

For colors, I'm deciding to build my own paint function for the hull panels rather than importing a pre-made panelled kit, so the palette stays distinct.

Now I'm laying out the front details: a recessed grille box with slat bars in cyan-steel tones framed by glowing accents, plus amber headlight boxes with dark housings and bracket details, and magenta fog strips alongside.

I'm positioning the bumper with hazard-stripe texturing, adding a bull-bar with angled uprights and a crossbar in front, and placing a half-torus tow hook centered at the base.

Next I'm adding magenta fog-light strips flanking the bumper, then applying a hood decal with the emblem texture, carefully setting the orientation vectors so the artwork projects correctly onto the sloped hood surface facing toward the cab.

I'm also adding small front mud guard wedges over the fenders and planning rod-style side mirrors extending from the cab.

Still placing details: mirror arms and bodies near the cab sides, thin glowing cyan trim rods along the hood's top edges, and a dark chassis frame box reinforcing the front underside.

For the hood itself I'm adding vent boxes with slats, angled corner armor plates, a tow-hook, headlight brackets, and small amber turn signals, while skipping the license plate decal since rivets are already implied by the panel texture. Working out how to apply the part/rod helper functions with consistent bone attachments and color strings for the darker grille sections.

For the windscreen I'm using a textured plane with a cyan HUD rendered on a dark glass background to keep it opaque, tilted slightly and sized to fit the cab, plus a slim cyan rod accent above it rather than a full frame to keep the geometry lightweight.

I'm drafting the buildCabShell function signature using the Ctx type from the module, following the template's destructuring pattern, and starting to plan the cab box dimensions with x spanning ±1.4 and y at 1.

For the geometry, I'm working out how the roof should slope to accommodate the turret ring, deciding on a raised rear hump and a sloped windscreen toward the nose so the roof height transitions from 2.5 down to meet the turret base around 2.3-2.35. I'm sketching the construction as a lower hull box, then a narrower upper greenhouse box offset inward in x and z to form the windscreen area, using simple box geometry with flat shading.

I'm now outlining the cab's side profile as a 2D silhouette in z-y coordinates that I'll extrude along x, defining points for the lower body, upper cab walls, and the roof hump, then setting up the windows as separate textured planes on the sides.

I'm placing the rear glowing screen facing outward, then adding door panels with hazard stripe texture near the sills and small handle details for the side doors.

For the windshield, since the extruded cab body is solid, I decide against true interior visibility and instead plan a simplified greenhouse structure built from pillars and a roof slab, with glass panes on the sides and suggestive seat/dashboard shapes rather than a fully hollow cabin.

Working out the windscreen glass geometry...

Still placing cab components...

I'm adjusting the hump height to 2.4 so the spotlight bar sits cleanly at 2.4–2.5 without exceeding the box, placing it near the front edge facing forward. Then I'm adding rear-corner antennas with glowing red tips, checking their height fits within bounds, before moving on to exhaust stacks.

For the stacks, I realize placing them directly behind the cab collides with the pod's bounding box, so I'm repositioning them to the outer sides of the cab at x ±1.5, z 0.85, running vertically from y1.3 to 2.6 with mounting brackets to avoid the overlap.

Then I plan a rear-wall screen facing -Z on the hump, and listing the texture set I need: hazard stripes, window glass reflections, rear screen, dash display, door decal numbers, and emblems, with glow applied to screens and lights. I'm also settling on colors, mostly drawing from the existing palette with a few custom additions.

I'm writing a box-creation helper function, then defining the hull paint with panel grooves, rivets, and grime accumulation near the bottom using noise-based color mixing.

Now I'm positioning the lower body chassis, front wheel arches, and door cutouts—setting coordinates for wheel wells and window/door openings along the lower body section.

I'm adding door trim lines, a steel handle box, and a hazard-stripe sill plane with a stretched repeating texture, then placing armor plates with hazard corners and rivet detailing on the cab's side hump before adding a side decal number.

Now I'm deciding to label the hump plate "AEGIS-7" instead of a door number, and working through plane orientation so the text reads correctly from both sides when viewed along the X axis.

For windows, I'm placing small glass planes at x ±1.3 with dark teal textures suggesting diagonal cyan reflection streaks, sized to fit between the roofline at 2.22 and body top at 1.9.

I could make the glass mostly transparent with alpha cutout, drawing only the opaque reflection streaks and leaving the rest see-through so the interior is visible underneath. The windscreen gets a similar streak treatment, and now I'm adding interior seats as small boxes positioned symmetrically at x ±.5.

Now I'm laying out the dashboard with glowing screen panels tilted to face the driver, plus a center console and a small steering wheel torus, figuring out positioning so everything fits inside the roofline without clipping.

Then I'm adding exterior trim details: hazard stripe strips on the roof hump and edges, plus planning for vent boxes, a beacon light, and a spotlight bar on the roof.

Positioning the spotlight bar and five amber lights at the front of the hump, deciding to skip a duplicate turret ring collar since the turret part already has one, and confirming the chassis covers the lower body underside.

Now adding amber marker lights on the front corners, cyan neon edge rods along the lower body's top edge, and a rear screen on the hump wall with a cyan graph texture and glowing frame, working out the sizing against the hump and lower body wall heights.

Still placing details... roof rails with end stanchions, antenna rods at the hump rear corners with glowing red tips, and exhaust stack cylinders positioned beside the hump.

Now I'm planning the heat shield rings and angled caps on the stacks, then moving to texture generation—building a yellow-and-black hazard stripe SVG pattern stretched as an instance plane.

For the geometry helpers, I'm setting up a glow wrapper that works on textured planes, a flat-part option for the box rendering, and a hazard-plane helper that orients stripes along the correct normal axis. I'm also sketching out the sloped front hump armor plate using an extruded wedge profile rather than a simple box.

Now I'm positioning the A-pillar rods, the roof slab and windscreen plane, and figuring out how the hump's front face doubles as the B-pillar so the rear roof gap lines up correctly with the window geometry.

Roof width 2.7 against lower body 2.8 works fine. I'll apply the same hull paint panelling to the lower body and hump, and a slightly lighter panelled finish to the roof slab — then just use the Ctx type as given rather than redeclaring it, since the module already provides it.

I'm checking the tread block geometry and rotation math to make sure the radial orientation around the wheel's x-axis matches the angle of each block correctly.

Since the mesh rotation is defined in bone-local space rather than model space, computing a simple rotation.x offset is unreliable here. I'll scrap the manual rotation lines and instead compute a proper quaternion from the axis-angle directly, passing that into the part setup instead of the old rotation/mesh assignments.

I need to fix the pieces sticking outside the wheel box. Checking the axle and box dimensions, the wheel fits fine, but the mud guard hazard lip extends past the box depth, so I'm adjusting its z-offset from the axle to pull it back inside.

The mud flap at the current z-offset also overshoots—I'll bring it closer to the axle along with the matching strip. Then I'm checking the guard arch plates, which push above the allowed y-height due to their radius and arc center; I'll shrink the radius and lower the center so the max extent stays within bounds, while confirming the z-extent of the arch sine curve stays fine. Now I need to locate these specific lines to make the edits.

I need to fix the overshoot where the hatch beacon sits too high relative to the shell and box boundaries, so I'm adjusting the shell width and lowering the hatch lid position to bring everything within bounds.

I also need to fix the chain and ratchet positions that extend past the 15cm tolerance—shifting the chain's x offset relative to the shell width, shrinking the torus radius slightly, and tightening the y-spacing so the anchor box and chain links stay within acceptable limits.

I need to fit the turret ring within the available bounding box, so I'm reducing the ring radius to around 0.4 so it stays within z 1.5 to 2.3, and reconsidering whether to shrink the whole turret assembly or just adjust the housing position at cz=1.9.

I'm scaling the ring down to 0.7 and adjusting bolts accordingly, then working through the barrel geometry — shortening barrel length, muzzle position, torus rings, and amber accent boxes to fit within the shrunk depth of gz+0.55. I also need to shorten the antenna height from 3.5 to around 3.08-3.1 and reposition the warning light sphere so it doesn't poke outside the bounding box.

Now I'm nudging the antenna rod and sloped top heights down slightly, checking the warning light placement relative to cz, and adjusting the right-side ammo box and belt positions so nothing exceeds the max x bound of 0.59.
